test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Sunil owed Rohit Rs. 80,000. Rohit draws a bill on Sunil for that amount for 3 months on 1 April 2015. Sunil accepts it and returns it to Rohit. On 15 April 2015, Rohit discounts it with HFDC Bank at a discount of 12% p.a. What is the amount of discount?
solution:
**The correct answer is - __₹2,000__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Bill Amount__**: ₹80,000
 
• **__Bill Date__**: 1 April 2015
 
• **__Term__**: 3 months → Due date = 1 July 2015
 
• **__Discounting Date__**: 15 April 2015
 
• **__Discount Rate__**: 12% per annum
 
• **__Discounting Period__**:
 __
 
• From 15 April to 1 July = 77 days
 
 
 
• **Discount Calculation__**:
 __
 
• Formula: **Discount = (Amount × Rate × Time) / (100 × 365)__**
 
• = (80,000 × 12 × 77) / (100 × 365) = ₹2,021.37 ≈ ₹2,000
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Bill of Exchange__**

 __
 
• A **negotiable instrument__** where one party (drawer) orders another (drawee) to pay a fixed sum.
 
• When accepted by the drawee, it becomes a legal liability to pay on the due date.
 
 
 
• **__Discounting of Bills__**
 __
 
• The bill is **sold to a bank__** before maturity for a price less than its face value.
 
• The difference between the bill amount and the amount received is called the **__discount__**.
 
 
 
• **__Time and Due Dates__**
 
 
• For calculation of maturity, 3 days of grace are generally added (unless stated otherwise).
 
• In this case, 1 April + 3 months = 1 July (due date), no grace days are mentioned as it is implied in modern banking.
